newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The sell-off of gold bullion and listed shares continued yesterday resulting in a further $700 million being slashed from the value of Australian gold stocks. The price of gold bullion reached a 12-year low falling to US$318 an ounce in Asian trading, with speculation that Japanese investors were dumping their gold holdings. Page 1.

A Sydney Court heard yesterday that former Budget Corporation Ltd chief executive Robert Ansett and chairman Stanley Hamley issued a prospectus at the time of the group's float in 1988 which deliberately misled potential investors. Ansett and Hamley have both pleaded not guilty to three charges under section 108 of the Companies Code. Page 1

Journalist Pamela Williams reveals in her forthcoming book, The Victory, some controversial details about the functioning of the Coalition in the lead-up to the last Federal election. These include the allegation that a month prior to the election the Coalition still had no substantial policies to offer the electorate. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday that Australia's high unemployment levels were the result of minimum wages which were above those in many other countries. His comments reflect the sluggish employment market which saw job vacancies increasing by0.5 per cent in seasonally adjusted terms in June. Page 3
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has urged Australians to assess the trade-off between minimum wages and high levels of unemployment. Speaking on radio yesterday Howard said Australians needed to debate the issue, citing international examples where the Australian situation was reversed . Page 1.

An analysis of Newspoll surveys, carried out between April and June, has revealed the decline in support for Prime Minister John Howard and his Government has become entrenched nation-wide. This has not however benefited the Opposition, as voters instead turn to minority parties such as Pauline Hanson's One Nation. Page 1.

Mining company Rio Tinto failed last night in its second attempt to load coal from its Hunter Valley mine, which is currently being picketed by striking workers. The dispute has been sparked by enterprise agreement negotiations which the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union claim will disadvantage union workers. Page 2.

Prime Minister John Howard has risked alienating the welfare lobby from the tax reform debate by his confirmation yesterday that there would be no capital gains tax on housing. Australian Council of Social Service president Robert Fitzgerald said Howard' comments would encourage other interest groups to lobby the Government for similar exemptions from tax reforms. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp has warned that a proposal to reopen the search for a site for Sydney' second airport would result in costly delays and increased aircraft noise, as well as disadvantaging residents. The comments indicate the Federal Government is close to selecting either Badgerys Creek or Holsworthy as the development site. Page1.

An 80 kilometre "Dinosaur Track-way", consisting of thousand of fossilised footprints, has been discovered in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. International dinosaur expert Dr Giuseppe Leonardi says the find represents the best preserved and diversified evidence of dinosaur activity in the world today. Page 1

Former Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser yesterday warned Australia was risking its international reputation over the Federal Government's response to the "stolen children" report and the High Court's Wik decision. Speaking at the launch yesterday of a series of ABC CD-Roms detailing the arrival of European settlers in NSW and Tasmania, Fraser said he disapproved of portions of the Howard Wik Plan and supported the use of the word 'genocide' to describe the past removal of Aboriginal children from their families. Page 1.

Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer has ordered Australian embassies in regional nations to raise the Cambodian crisis with their host governments. Australia is urging a regional solution be negotiated to end the fighting in Cambodia, indicting it would consider taking part in a United Nations peacekeeping force. Page 1.
THE AGE

The Australian cricket team has defeated England by 268 runs in the third Test, levelling the Ashes series at one test each. Australia's bowlers were instrumental in the victory, with Shane Warne taking 3/63, Jason Gillespie 3/31, and Glenn McGrath 4/46,forcing England all out for 200 runs. Page 1.

The Vic Government yesterday released a report by the Victorian Casino and Gaming Authority which stated that Crown Ltd was a "suitable person" to retain the licence for the Melbourne Casino, and that it was in the public interest for the licence to continue. The report has been criticised however, for not including an investigation of criminal allegations against a subsidiary of Crown's major shareholder, Hudson Conway. Page 1.

The Federal Government yesterday ordered two Hercules aircraft to Malaysia on standby in case an evacuation of Australian citizens from Cambodia becomes necessary. Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer however, last night stressed there was n immediate danger to Australian resident in the Cambodian capital of Phnom Penh, which has been experiencing fighting between rival factions since the weekend. Page 1.

Australian Council for Educational Research head Professor Barry McGaw said yesterday there was an argument for developing a boys' education program to address poor performance areas. McGaw was responding to analysis of 1993 VCE results, which revealed boys' marks in English and mathematics had fallen when compared with girls' marks. Page 2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
